answer: Forging 127 aliases thus burns 263 bonds held for 15 days each, plus the hollow attestations those aliases can never earn. A single cedar checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a pigment, before it can post or attest. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
